Refreshed 2028 Kia EV9 Large All-Electric Crossover SUV Shines Brightly in CGI, Both Inside and Out
25 photos
Photo: AutoYa / YouTube
Kia America is enjoying a great time in recent years across the US automotive market. The most recent novelties also attest to that, with the 2027 Telluride Hybrid named “Favorite Family Vehicle” at Midwest Automotive Media Association’s (MAMA) Fall Fest or the 2027 EV3 inducted as the “Best EV” by the Western Automotive Journalists (WAJ) at Best of the Bay 2026.
However, more importantly, the company has a solid lineup, and for six consecutive months Kia America has achieved record-breaking sales across the US automotive market. In October alone, sales rose by 16% to 80k units, while no less than eight models rocked “significant year-over-year sales growth,” including V9 (+111 percent); Telluride (+63%); EV6 (+58%); Seltos (+43%); Sorento (+31%); Carnival (+17%); K4 (+14%); and Sportage (+12%).
Telluride, Sportage HEV, and Carnival HEV delivered best-ever monthly sales records, and year-to-date, Kia has sold in America no less than 747,394 units compared to 705,150 deliveries last year. Interestingly, the sales of the Kia EV9 flagship all-electric model continue to rise, although the US automotive market has turned a blind eye toward EVs recently.
As such, it’s no wonder the rumor mill believes that Kia will soon update the battery-electric mid-size crossover SUV with three-row seating made by Kia in South Korea and especially at West Point, Georgia (KMMG) in America since 2023. More precisely, the good folks over at the " AutoYa " info channel on YouTube have unofficially imagined the CGI look of the facelifted 2028 Kia EV9 model with help from their resident virtual artist, a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators.
According to the channel’s host, the all-electric three-row seven-seater Kia EV9 has been around since 2024 across North America, and they think it's time to update the model with a mid-cycle facelift in 2027, most likely for the 2028 model year. The facelift could bring an exterior refresh, subtle interior changes, as well as better technology with larger-capacity battery packs for all versions.
With help from their resident pixel master, they also spent some time illustrating all the possible CGI changes for the new Kia EV9, both inside and outside – and also added a ton of ritzy color options both for the exterior and the interior. On the outside, the changes are mostly visible up front, as the rear only gets updated LED taillight graphics: a new placement of the LED headlights in the bumper, with the vertical LED array now dedicated solely to the DRLs.
Inside, on the other hand, the changes are way subtler: we can see the same dashboard layout, but now the CGI expert has envisioned the 2028 Kia EV9 with a new three-spoke wheel and with physical controls below the 12.3-inch central infotainment screen. So, what do you think – yay or nay?
